concept.name: Pairs spread z-score strategy
concept.definition: A statistical-arbitrage rule that monitors the spread between two historically linked securities, standardizes it as a z-score against its own rolling mean and standard deviation, and enters a market-neutral long/short when the spread stretches beyond a threshold (commonly two standard deviations), exiting at reversion. It is the standardized-distance variant of the Gatev-Goetzmann-Rouwenhorst pairs rule.
concept.intuition: If two stocks usually move together, the times they do not are opportunities: when the gap is two standard deviations wide, history says it more often narrows than widens - so you short the leader and buy the laggard.
concept.mechanics: Estimate the spread (price ratio or hedge-ratio residual), compute z = (spread - rolling mean) / rolling sigma, open the pair when |z| exceeds the entry threshold, and close when z reverts toward zero or crosses the exit threshold. Gatev et al. (2006) match pairs by minimum distance between normalized price series and trade divergences beyond two historical standard deviations.
concept.formula: z_t = (s_t - mu_s) / sigma_s; enter short the spread if z_t > +2, long if z_t < -2, exit near z_t approx. 0.
concept.failure_modes: Structural breaks - a takeover, earnings regime change, or delisting - turn a stretched spread into a permanently repriced one while the z-score keeps signaling reversion, and rolling-window estimates degrade in volatility regime shifts.
concept.misconceptions: That a 2-sigma threshold makes the trade statistically safe; spread distributions are fat-tailed and non-stationary, so extreme readings cluster exactly when the pair relationship is breaking.
concept.example: Two retail stocks' price-ratio spread has mean 1.00 and sigma 0.02; when the spread hits 1.05 (z = 2.5), short the outperformer and buy the underperformer dollar-neutral, exiting when the spread returns to 1.01.

citations.source: Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst, 'Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative Value Arbitrage Rule' (SSRN; published RFS 2006)
